description: Single-panel double-logarithmic fatigue S–N plot (Δσ/2–2Nf curves, Fig. 5) for the ST and aged Fe-30.5Mn-8Al-1C steel. The x-axis is "Number of reversals to fracture /2Nf" on a logarithmic scale running from roughly 5×10^4 to beyond 10^7, with major gridlines labelled 10^5, 10^6 and 10^7; the y-axis is "Stress amplitude /MPa" from 140 to 340 in 20 MPa steps (the axis title is partially cropped at the upper left). Four marker-plus-line series are plotted: ST (green down-triangles), 550-6 (black squares), 600-6 (red circles) and 650-6 (blue up-triangles). Every series falls approximately linearly on the double-logarithmic coordinates between about 220 and 320 MPa and then flattens into a horizontal plateau at low stress amplitude; right-pointing arrows extend each plateau into the run-out region near 10^7–2×10^7 reversals. No numeric values are printed on the panel. From the pixels the plateau heights rank, highest to lowest, 600-6 > 650-6 > 550-6 > ST, the ST plateau sitting just above the 160 MPa gridline. The figure demonstrates that aging raises low-amplitude fatigue resistance, with 600-6 giving the highest fatigue strength.

subfigures.description: Log-log S–N (Δσ/2–2Nf) plot: stress amplitude /MPa (140–340, 20 MPa steps) versus number of reversals to fracture /2Nf (log scale, 10^5–10^7 gridlines). Four series with fitted lines: ST (green down-triangles), 550-6 (black squares), 600-6 (red circles), 650-6 (blue up-triangles); each shows a linear regime at high stress and a horizontal plateau at low stress, terminated by right-pointing run-out arrows near 10^7–2×10^7 reversals.

observations.observation: The panel is a double-logarithmic S–N plot with y-axis 'Stress amplitude /MPa' spanning 140 to 340 in 20 MPa increments and x-axis 'Number of reversals to fracture /2Nf' with labelled gridlines at 10^5, 10^6 and 10^7.
Four data series are plotted, distinguished by marker and line colour: green down-triangles for ST, black squares for 550-6, red circles for 600-6, and blue up-triangles for 650-6.
Each series is approximately linear in the double-logarithmic coordinates at high stress amplitude (roughly 220–320 MPa) and flattens into a horizontal plateau at low stress amplitude.
Right-pointing arrows terminate each curve at the far right near 10^7–2×10^7 reversals, marking run-out (non-failure) points.

The plateau (fatigue-limit) heights visible in the pixels rank from highest to lowest as 600-6 (red) > 650-6 (blue) > 550-6 (black) > ST (green), with the ST plateau lying just above the 160 MPa gridline and the 600-6 plateau approaching the 180 MPa gridline.
No numerical data labels are printed on the panel; all values must be read against the axis gridlines.
The caption identifies the figure as Δσ/2-2N curves for the ST, 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6 samples.
The citing text states the fatigue strength sustained for 10^7 cycles is 157.5 MPa for ST, 162 MPa for 550-6, 175.5 MPa for 600-6 and 171 MPa for 650-6.
The citing text states that at a given stress amplitude all aged samples exhibit longer fatigue lives than the ST sample.

The citing text states that the 550-6 condition has the longest fatigue lives among the aged samples at higher stress amplitudes, whereas near the fatigue limit the 600-6 condition attains the highest fatigue lives and fatigue strength.
The citing text reports that the fitted fatigue strength coefficient σ'f and exponent b, together with the root mean square error of log10 Nf, are summarised in Table 1 (not shown here).
The citing text links the longer fatigue lives of the 550-6 (at 315 MPa) and 600-6 (at 180 MPa) samples to the narrower fatigue striation spacing seen in Fig. 7.
